questions.question: A nickel is worth how many cents?
questions.explain: A nickel is worth 5 cents. Don't mix it up with the dime, which is 10 cents.

questions.question: A dime is worth how many cents?
questions.explain: A dime is worth 10 cents. A nickel is 5 and a quarter is 25, so keep them straight.

questions.question: A loonie is worth how many dollars?
questions.explain: A loonie is 1 dollar. A toonie is 2 dollars, so don't mix them up.

questions.question: A toonie is worth how many dollars?
questions.explain: A toonie is worth 2 dollars. A loonie is 1 dollar, so the toonie is worth more.

questions.question: Mia puts a quarter in her piggy bank. How many cents is it?
questions.explain: A quarter is worth 25 cents. Some kids say 20, but that is not right — it is 25.

questions.question: A quarter is worth more than a dime. How many cents more?
questions.explain: A quarter is 25 and a dime is 10, so 25 minus 10 is 15. The trap is thinking a quarter is 20.

questions.question: A loonie and a toonie together make how many dollars?
questions.explain: A loonie is 1 and a toonie is 2, so together they make 3 dollars. Don't just pick the toonie's value.

questions.question: A nickel is bigger than a dime. Which one is worth more?
questions.explain: A dime is worth 10 cents and a nickel is 5, so the dime is worth more. Big does not mean more here.

questions.question: A toonie is worth 2 dollars and a loonie is worth 1 dollar. A toonie is how many dollars more than a loonie?
questions.explain: A toonie is 2 and a loonie is 1, so 2 minus 1 is 1 dollar more. The trap is adding them to get 3.

questions.question: A sticker at the school store costs 10 cents. Which one coin can Ivy use to pay for it?
questions.explain: A dime is worth 10 cents, so one dime pays for the sticker. A nickel is the bigger coin, but it is worth only 5 cents.

questions.question: Ella has a toonie. Her brother has a loonie. Who has enough for a 2-dollar hot chocolate?
questions.explain: A toonie is worth 2 dollars, so Ella has just enough. A loonie is only 1 dollar, so her brother is still 1 dollar short.

questions.question: A big cookie at the bake sale costs 20 cents. Ruby has one quarter. Can she pay for the cookie?
questions.explain: A quarter is worth 25 cents, and 25 cents is more than 20 cents. Many children say a quarter is 20 cents or 10 cents, so remember the quarter is 25.

questions.question: Mia has a nickel, a dime, a quarter and a loonie in her pocket. Which one of her coins is worth the least?
questions.explain: A nickel is 5 cents, and that is less than a dime, a quarter or a loonie. The dime is the smallest coin, but a small coin can still be worth more.
